posts.big_note: The Fed's preferred inflation gauge in October — the hottest in 3 years
posts.headline: Inflation just hit a 3-year high — and now Wall Street expects the Fed to RAISE rates on Dec. 9, not cut them.
posts.source: Source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, October 2026 PCE report (Nov. 25, 2026)
posts.caption:
The relief everyone was waiting for just got put on hold.

The Fed's favorite inflation gauge — the PCE price index — rose 3.8% over the past year in October, its hottest reading in three years, up from 3.6% in September. Core PCE, which strips out food and energy, climbed to 3.3%. Prices rose 0.3% in just that one month.

With inflation that far above the Fed's 2% goal, markets have flipped: instead of a rate cut, Wall Street now prices in a rate INCREASE at the Dec. 9 meeting. The Fed's benchmark already sits at 3.75%–4.00%.

Why it's your money: card APRs, car loans and mortgage rates move with the Fed, so the cheaper-borrowing everyone hoped for in 2026 isn't coming — and could reverse. The one upside: high-yield savings keeps paying well.

My take: higher-for-longer stopped being a warning and became the bill. If you're carrying a balance, that's the line to attack first — a rate that isn't dropping costs you every single month.

Is a stubborn card or loan rate changing how you're spending this holiday season? 👇

Source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, October 2026 PCE report (released Nov. 25, 2026)
Educational only — not financial advice.
